roads.name: Pinery
words: Curve after curve after curve: 31 in 2.1 miles, about 15 a mile.
Plenty of tight curves among them.
The curves flow straight into one another.
From 586 to 601 ft, with 87 ft of up and down along the way.
roads.ratingNote: A full bar is top marks for that part; the percentages are each part's share of the rating. Curves, length and up and down are ranked against every road in the library. The rest are scored on the road itself: how few side roads join it, whether the curves or the limit set the pace, and how little is built up along it. At the 80 km/h limit its corners still ask for about 1.03 g, so the curves, not the limit, set the pace. Most of it has no posted limit on the map, so this takes Ontario's 80 km/h.

roads.name: Road 119 (Highway 7)
words: Sweeping and steady: 9 curves in 4.5 miles.
Tight and technical: most curves turn on a radius under 130 ft.
From 1,114 to 1,192 ft, with 163 ft of up and down along the way.

roads.name: Clarke Road
words: Sweeping and steady: 7 curves in 3.2 miles.
From 814 to 910 ft, with 246 ft of up and down along the way.
8 parks, trailheads and other stops along it, so it's likely busier than most, especially on weekends.
